Chief_Complaint.content: Patient presents with sore, red, and very itchy skin.
Chief_Complaint.source_text: I have like a sore, and a red skin. It's kind of, it's really itchy, and it's like super annoying.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Symptoms have been present for four days.
The rash is located on the chest, hands, and arms, particularly inside the elbows.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Uh, mostly like my chest, my, my hands, my arms. Like, like really... Just the chest, hands and like, like inside the elbows. Yeah.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The itching is severe, constant, and disrupts sleep and work focus.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I can't even sleep at night... when I'm in a meeting... I can't focus

History_of_Present_Illness.content: The skin is sore and cracked in some areas.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: you also mentioned it's been quite sore... my skin is a bit cracked in some parts

History_of_Present_Illness.content: There is no bleeding, pus, or discharge from the skin.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: You've not, haven't uh seen any other uh pus or blood, coming out of your skin. Patient: No.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient is not aware of any triggers and has not changed shower gel or clothing.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Are you aware of any triggers... No I I haven't

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient tried an over-the-counter steroid cream last night with no effect.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: I bought a, a steroid cream at the pharmacy last night. But it apparently didn't help

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient has also tried antihistamines recently without relief.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: Yes, I have tried antihistamines, uh lately, but it didn't really help.

History_of_Present_Illness.content: Patient denies any associated fevers, cough, or breathing difficulties.
History_of_Present_Illness.source_text: No. just very itchy. Nothing else... Your chest is OK? No cough, no breathing difficulties? Patient: No.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient has a history of eczema.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Uh earlier I was like prescribed for my eczema.

Past_Medical_History.content: Patient had asthma in the past but does not anymore.
Past_Medical_History.source_text: Uh, no. I just had asthma in the past. But not anymore.

Medications.source_text: And do you take any regular medications at the moment? Patient: Uh no.

Adverse_Drug_Reactions_and_Allergies.source_text: Uh do you have any allergies at all? Patient: Ohh, allergies. Uh, no.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient is 31 years old, lives with flatmates, and works as a project manager at a pharmaceutical company.
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I'm thirty one... I live with a few flatmates... I work uh at a pharmaceutical company... I'm a, like a kind of project manager.
do you smoke at all? Patient: No.

Social_and_Family_History.content: Patient drinks alcohol socially (a few beers per week).
Social_and_Family_History.source_text: I'd say a few, a few beers per week. Something like this.

Assessment.content: The impression is a flare-up of eczema.

Plan_of_Care.content: Use the steroids and emollients for the next seven to ten days.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: using that for the first seven to ten days.

Plan_of_Care.content: Trial a stronger antihistamine, such as Fexofenadine, for itching.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: I can give you something a little bit stronger today as well... something like Fexofenadine

Plan_of_Care.content: Advised to keep a trigger diary for potential irritants like shower gels or clothing.
Plan_of_Care.source_text: it's also worth keeping a diary of any triggers which are affecting your symptoms

Follow_up_Information.content: Patient to return for review in one week to ten days if symptoms do not improve or if they worsen.
Follow_up_Information.source_text: do come back and see me next week, if things don't get better.
